solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option B: permanent tissues

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Permanent tissues having all cells similar in structure and function are called simple tissues.
Statement II: In flowering plants, xylem fibres are the main water-transporting elements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Permanent tissues having all cells similar in structure and function are called simple tissues; those with many different types of cells are complex tissues. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements. Xylem fibres have highly thickened walls and obliterated central lumens.
steps: Statement II: false, tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent Tissues; Xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls.
Statement II: Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering, cylindrical cells that have dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells closely associated with sieve tube elements; the two are connected by pit fields present between their common longitudinal walls. Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering cylindrical cells which have dense cytoplasm and a nucleus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following belong to the ground tissue system of primary stems and roots?

(a) Cortex
(b) Pericycle
(c) Pith
(d) Phloem
(e) Epidermis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and the vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. Parenchymatous cells of the ground tissue are usually present in the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays in primary stems and roots. Phloem belongs to the vascular tissue system and the epidermis to the epidermal tissue system.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) include a tissue of another tissue system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (The Ground Tissue System)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (meristem) with List-II (position).

List-I:
A. Root apical meristem
B. Shoot apical meristem
C. Intercalary meristem
D. Lateral meristem

List-II:
I. Cylindrical meristem in the mature regions of roots and shoots, lateral in position
II. Between mature tissues, as in grasses
III. Distant-most region of the stem axis
IV. Tip of the root

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The root apical meristem occupies the tip of a root, while the shoot apical meristem occupies the distant-most region of the stem axis. Intercalary meristems occur between mature tissues, as in grasses. Lateral meristems appear later, in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants, particularly those that produce woody axes, and are lateral and cylindrical.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange the two apical meristems, or the intercalary and lateral meristems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Meristematic Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Xylem and phloem are described as complex tissues.
Reason (R): Each is made up of more than one type of cell, and these cells work together as a unit.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells that work together as a unit. Xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres, xylem parenchyma) and phloem (sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, phloem fibres) are the complex tissues in plants. R is the defining reason.
steps: More than one cell type working as a unit → complex tissue → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Complex Tissues)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cortex of a dicot stem consists of three sub-zones. Which of the following gives them in the correct order from outside inwards?

solution.explanation: The outer hypodermis has a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis. Below it are the cortical layers of rounded, thin-walled parenchyma with conspicuous intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is the endodermis (starch sheath). The pericycle lies inside the endodermis and is not part of the cortex.
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option is the reverse order. The second places the endodermis in the middle, but it is the innermost layer. The third includes the pericycle, which lies inside the endodermis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dicotyledonous Stem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Hypodermis, cortical layers, endodermis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about xylem are correct?

(a) Tracheids are dead and without protoplasm; the inner layers of their walls have thickenings that vary in form.
(b) Vessel members are devoid of protoplasm.
(c) Xylem conducts water and minerals from the leaves to the stem and roots.
(d) Besides conduction, xylem provides mechanical strength to plant parts.
(e) A vessel member has lignified walls and a large central cavity.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Xylem functions as a conducting tissue for water and minerals from the roots to the stem and leaves, and also provides mechanical strength. Tracheids are elongated, dead cells without protoplasm, with thick lignified walls whose inner layers bear thickenings of various forms. A vessel is a long cylindrical tube of many vessel members, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity; vessel members are devoid of protoplasm.
steps: (c) false: from roots to stem and leaves
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (c), which reverses the direction of conduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Xylem)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a dicot root, both the tangential and the radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of a water-impermeable, waxy material in the form of Casparian strips.
Statement II: In a dicot stem, the cortical layers below the hypodermis consist of rounded, thin-walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In the dicot root, the tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy suberin as Casparian strips. In the dicot stem, the cortical layers below the hypodermis are rounded, thin-walled parenchymatous cells with conspicuous intercellular spaces.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dicotyledonous Root; Dicotyledonous Stem)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the vascular bundles are all of nearly similar size.
Reason (R): The size of a vascular bundle depends on the size of the vein, and the veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In a dorsiventral leaf, the size of the vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins, and the veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of dicot leaves; so the bundles vary in size and A is false. Vascular bundles of nearly similar size (except the main veins) are a feature of the isobilateral (monocot) leaf with parallel venation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dorsiventral (Dicot) Leaf)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes collenchyma in relation to the dicot stem?

options.text: It forms semi-lunar patches above the phloem as part of the pericycle
It forms the sclerenchymatous hypodermis found in monocot stems
It occurs in layers below the epidermis, as a homogeneous layer or in patches, and the collenchymatous hypodermis gives mechanical strength to the young stem
It consists of dead cells with lignified walls that lack intercellular spaces

solution.explanation: Collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants, either as a homogeneous layer or in patches. In the dicot stem, the hypodermis consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis, which provide mechanical strength to the young stem.
steps: Collenchyma: below epidermis in dicots, homogeneous layer or patches
Dicot stem hypodermis = collenchyma → strength to young stem
solution.why_others_wrong: The semi-lunar patches of the pericycle are sclerenchyma. The hypodermis of the monocot stem is sclerenchymatous, not collenchymatous. Collenchyma cells are living, with walls thickened at the corners by cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, not lignin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Collenchyma); Dicotyledonous Stem
solution.final_answer: Option C: It occurs in layers below the epidermis, as a homogeneous layer or in patches, and the collenchymatous hypodermis gives mechanical strength to the young stem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae and:

options.text: mycoplasma and PPLO (pleuro pneumonia like organisms)

solution.explanation: The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma and PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms).
steps: Prokaryotes: bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma, PPLO
solution.why_others_wrong: Yeast (a fungus), Amoeba, Euglena, Chlamydomonas, diatoms and desmids are all eukaryotes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option C: mycoplasma and PPLO (pleuro pneumonia like organisms)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In both plant and animal cells, the main arena of cellular activities, where various chemical reactions keep the cell in the 'living state', is the:

solution.explanation: The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells. Various chemical reactions occur in it to keep the cell in the 'living state'.
steps: Main arena of cellular activities → cytoplasm
solution.why_others_wrong: The nucleus holds the genetic material, the cell wall gives shape and protection, and the vacuole stores water, sap and materials not useful for the cell.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', An Overview of Cell
solution.final_answer: Option A: cytoplasm

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Ribosomes are:

options.text: composed of DNA and proteins, and surrounded by a single membrane
composed of RNA and proteins, and not surrounded by any membrane
composed of lipids and proteins, and surrounded by a double membrane
composed of RNA and lipids, and surrounded by a single membrane

solution.explanation: Ribosomes are granular structures first observed under the electron microscope by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ribosomes contain RNA, not DNA, and are not membrane-bound; every wrong option adds a membrane or a wrong component.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Ribosomes)
solution.final_answer: Option B: composed of RNA and proteins, and not surrounded by any membrane

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures in the cytoplasm, collectively called the cytoskeleton, consists of:

options.text: cristae, matrix and the outer membrane

solution.explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. It is involved in mechanical support, motility and maintenance of cell shape.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cisternae and vesicles describe the Golgi apparatus and ER, cristae and matrix the mitochondrion, and grana and stroma the chloroplast.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cytoskeleton)
solution.final_answer: Option D: microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Animal cells have centrioles, which are absent in almost all plant cells.
Statement II: Plant cells possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT's comparison of plant and animal cells: plant cells possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole, which are absent in animal cells; animal cells have centrioles, which are absent in almost all plant cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Normally there is one nucleus per cell. Which of the following are cited by NCERT as mature cells that lack a nucleus?

options.text: Nerve cells and white blood cells
Erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants
Mesophyll cells and root hair cells

solution.explanation: Normally there is only one nucleus per cell, though variations in the number of nuclei are frequently observed. Some mature cells even lack a nucleus, e.g., erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants.
steps: Mature cells without nucleus: mammalian erythrocytes, sieve tube cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Companion cells, guard cells, nerve cells, white blood cells, mesophyll cells and root hair cells all have a nucleus. (The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the nucleus of the companion cell.)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Nucleus)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Erythrocytes of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Plasmodesmata are pores in the nuclear envelope through which RNA moves into the cytoplasm.
Statement II: The cell wall helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides a barrier to undesirable macromolecules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The cell wall and middle lamellae may be traversed by plasmodesmata, which connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells; the passages for RNA in the nuclear envelope are nuclear pores. Besides giving shape and protecting the cell from mechanical damage and infection, the cell wall helps in cell-to-cell interaction and provides a barrier to undesirable macromolecules.
steps: Statement I: false, plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cell Wall)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of the cell) with List-II (what it contains).

List-I:
A. Mitochondrial matrix
B. Thylakoids
C. Chloroplast stroma
D. Vacuole

List-II:
I. Water, sap, excretory products and other materials not useful for the cell
II. Single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules and 70S ribosomes
III. Enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins
IV. Chlorophyll pigments

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The mitochondrial matrix possesses a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and components for protein synthesis. The chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids. The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. The vacuole contains water, sap, excretory products and other materials not useful for the cell.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the matrix with the stroma, the thylakoids with the stroma, or the stroma with the vacuole.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Mitochondria; Plastids; Vacuoles)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The number of mitochondria per cell is variable.
Reason (R): The number of mitochondria in a cell depends on the physiological activity of the cell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the number of mitochondria per cell is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells. R states the cause of the variation in A.
steps: Number depends on activity → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Mitochondria)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the cell membrane are correct?

(a) The lipid component of the membrane mainly consists of phosphoglycerides.
(b) Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by simple diffusion along the concentration gradient.
(c) Chemical studies on human red blood cells enabled scientists to deduce the possible structure of the plasma membrane.
(d) The detailed structure of the membrane was worked out with the light microscope, long before the electron microscope came into use.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent of the electron microscope in the 1950s. Chemical studies on the cell membrane, especially in human RBCs, enabled scientists to deduce its possible structure. The lipid component mainly consists of phosphoglycerides. Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by simple diffusion along the concentration gradient.
steps: (d) false: the electron microscope was needed
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes the false statement (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cell Membrane)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Compared with the ribosomes in the cytoplasm of a plant cell, the ribosomes of its chloroplasts are:

options.text: larger, of the 80S type, while the cytoplasmic ones are 70S
smaller, of the 70S type, while the cytoplasmic ones are 80S
absent, since chloroplasts import all their proteins

solution.explanation: The stroma of the chloroplast contains small, double-stranded circular DNA molecules and ribosomes. The ribosomes of the chloroplasts are smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ribosomes (80S).
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option reverses the two types. Chloroplast ribosomes are not 80S, and they are not absent: the stroma contains ribosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Plastids)
solution.final_answer: Option B: smaller, of the 70S type, while the cytoplasmic ones are 80S

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: From his studies on plant tissues, Schwann concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.
Statement II: The cell theory as formulated by Schleiden and Schwann explained how new cells are formed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Schwann concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of plant cells. Schleiden and Schwann together formulated the cell theory, but it did not explain how new cells were formed. Rudolf Virchow later explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
steps: Statement II: false, the theory did not explain how new cells are formed
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Theory
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about centrioles, cilia and flagella are correct?

(a) Centrioles form the basal bodies of cilia and flagella.
(b) In animal cells, centrioles give rise to the spindle fibres that form the spindle apparatus during cell division.
(c) The peripheral fibrils of a centriole are made of the protein tubulin.
(d) The adjacent peripheral triplets of a centriole are not linked to one another.
(e) Cilia and flagella are covered with plasma membrane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A centriole has an organisation like a cartwheel: nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, each a triplet, and the adjacent triplets are also linked. Centrioles form the basal body of cilia or flagella, and the spindle fibres that give rise to the spindle apparatus during cell division in animal cells. Cilia and flagella are covered with plasma membrane.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain the false statement. (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Cilia and Flagella; Centrosome and Centrioles)
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The lumen of a mitochondrion is divided into two aqueous compartments, the outer compartment and the matrix.
Reason (R): The outer membrane of a mitochondrion forms a number of infoldings called cristae.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Each mitochondrion is bound by two membranes, which divide its lumen into two aqueous compartments: the outer compartment and the inner compartment, the matrix. The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary; it is the inner membrane that forms the infoldings called cristae towards the matrix.
steps: R: false (cristae are infoldings of the inner membrane)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Mitochondria)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mitochondria and chloroplasts are parts of the endomembrane system, because their functions are coordinated with those of the ER and the Golgi complex.
Reason (R): The functions of the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles are coordinated, so these are considered together as the endomembrane system.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles are considered together as the endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated. The functions of mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not coordinated with these components, so they are not considered part of the endomembrane system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells (Endomembrane System)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which observation best supports the view that the cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms?

options.text: Every cell has a cell wall, a nucleus and chloroplasts
Unicellular organisms can exist independently and perform the essential functions of life, while anything less than a complete cell does not ensure independent living
All cells are of the same size and shape, whatever their function
Cells can be seen only with the electron microscope

solution.concept: Cell as the unit of life
solution.explanation: Unicellular organisms are capable of (i) independent existence and (ii) performing the essential functions of life. Anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living. Hence the cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
steps: Nothing less than a cell lives independently
solution.why_others_wrong: Animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts, and some mature cells lack a nucleus. Cells vary greatly in size and shape with function. Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell, long before the electron microscope existed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', What is a Cell?
solution.final_answer: Option B: Unicellular organisms can exist independently and perform the essential functions of life, while anything less than a complete cell does not ensure independent living

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (membrane covering).

List-I:
A. Ribosome
B. Vacuole
C. Mitochondrion
D. Nucleus

List-II:
I. Double-membrane envelope with pores
II. Not surrounded by any membrane
III. Two membranes, the inner one folded into cristae
IV. A single membrane, the tonoplast

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ribosomes are not surrounded by any membrane. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane, the tonoplast. A mitochondrion has two membranes, the inner one forming infoldings called cristae. The nucleus has a nuclear envelope of two parallel membranes, interrupted by nuclear pores.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes give the ribosome a membrane, or swap the two double-membrane structures, or give the vacuole two membranes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Eukaryotic Cells
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Cells that do not divide further enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage (G0). They enter it by exiting which phase of the cell cycle?

solution.explanation: Cells that do not divide further exit the G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called the quiescent stage (G0) of the cell cycle.
solution.why_others_wrong: A cell that has passed into S or G2 has begun preparing for division; NCERT describes the exit to G0 from G1. M phase is the division itself.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of Cell Cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option B: G1 phase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During zygotene of meiotic prophase I, the complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a:

solution.explanation: During zygotene, homologous chromosomes start pairing (synapsis). The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad; these are more clearly visible at the next stage, pachytene.
solution.why_others_wrong: A chiasma is the X-shaped site of crossing over seen in diplotene. A kinetochore is the disc-shaped structure on the centromere. A dyad of cells is formed after telophase I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I: Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option A: bivalent or tetrad

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is called the:

solution.explanation: The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed the cell cycle.
steps: Genome duplication + synthesis of constituents + division = cell cycle
solution.why_others_wrong: Cytokinesis is division of the cytoplasm and karyokinesis division of the nucleus; both are only parts of M phase. Interkinesis is the short stage between meiosis I and meiosis II.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: cell cycle

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Each meiocyte that completes meiosis forms four haploid cells. How many meiocytes must complete meiosis to produce 400 haploid cells?

solution.explanation: Meiosis involves two sequential nuclear and cell divisions, and four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II. So the number of meiocytes needed is 400 ÷ 4 = 100.
solution.why_others_wrong: 400 assumes one cell per meiocyte. 200 stops after meiosis I (two cells per meiocyte). 1600 multiplies by 4 instead of dividing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option C: 100

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A single cell divides repeatedly by mitosis until 64 cells are formed. Each division of a cell produces two cells. How many individual cell divisions take place in all?

solution.explanation: Each division turns one cell into two, so it adds exactly one cell to the total. Going from 1 cell to 64 cells therefore needs 64 − 1 = 63 divisions. Check by rounds: 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 = 63 divisions in 6 rounds.
solution.shortcut: Cells formed − 1 = number of divisions.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 is the number of rounds (generations) of division, not the number of divisions. 32 counts only the divisions of the last round. 64 is the number of cells formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Mitosis (Significance of Mitosis)
solution.final_answer: Option D: 63

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the S and G2 phases, the new DNA molecules formed are not distinct but intertwined.
Statement II: In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by a furrow in the plasma membrane that gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre, dividing the cytoplasm into two.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In the S and G2 phases the new DNA molecules formed are not distinct but intertwined; they condense into mitotic chromosomes in prophase. In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane, which gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Prophase; Cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In plant cells, cytokinesis takes place by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane.
Reason (R): Plant cells are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Plant cells are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, so they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism: wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls (cell plate). The furrow is the method of animal cells. A is false, R is true.
steps: A: false (plant cells form a cell plate)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about prophase of mitosis are correct?

(a) The chromosomal material condenses to form compact mitotic chromosomes.
(b) Chromosomes are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the centromere.
(c) Prophase follows the S and G2 phases of interphase.
(d) The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of prophase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Prophase follows the S and G2 phases. It is marked by the initiation of condensation of the chromosomal material into compact mitotic chromosomes, each composed of two chromatids attached at the centromere. The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of the second phase, metaphase.
steps: (d) false: it marks the start of metaphase
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes the false statement (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Prophase; Metaphase)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In metaphase I of meiosis, the microtubules from the opposite poles of the spindle attach to:

options.text: the two sister chromatids of each chromosome

solution.explanation: In metaphase I, the bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate, and the microtubules from the opposite poles of the spindle attach to the pair of homologous chromosomes. (In mitotic metaphase and metaphase II they attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.)
steps: Metaphase I: spindle fibres from opposite poles → the two homologues of each bivalent
solution.why_others_wrong: Attachment to sister chromatids from opposite poles happens in mitosis and in metaphase II. The nuclear envelope and nucleolus have disappeared by the end of diakinesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Metaphase I)
solution.final_answer: Option C: the pair of homologous chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Meiosis produces the diploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms, while fertilisation restores the haploid phase.
Statement II: The first two stages of prophase I are relatively short-lived compared with pachytene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Meiosis ensures the production of the haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms, whereas fertilisation restores the diploid phase; Statement I reverses them. The first two stages of prophase I (leptotene and zygotene) are relatively short-lived compared with the next stage, pachytene.
steps: Statement I: false (meiosis → haploid; fertilisation → diploid)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of meiosis) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Pachytene
B. Diplotene
C. Diakinesis
D. Telophase II

List-II:
I. Chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologues for separation
II. The two groups of chromosomes are again enclosed by a nuclear envelope, and cytokinesis gives a tetrad of four haploid cells
III. Bivalent chromosomes now clearly appear as tetrads
IV. The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other, except at the sites of crossovers

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Pachytene: bivalents clearly appear as tetrads, and recombination nodules appear. Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and the recombined homologues tend to separate except at the crossovers (chiasmata). Diakinesis: chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. Telophase II: the two groups of chromosomes are enclosed by nuclear envelopes and cytokinesis gives a tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid daughter cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap pachytene with diplotene, diakinesis with telophase II, or pachytene with diakinesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I; Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Consider these events of meiotic prophase I: (i) terminalisation of chiasmata; (ii) appearance of recombination nodules; (iii) dissolution of the synaptonemal complex; (iv) formation of the synaptonemal complex. Which is the correct order in which they occur?

solution.explanation: Zygotene: synapsis with formation of the synaptonemal complex (iv). Pachytene: recombination nodules appear, marking the sites of crossing over (ii). Diplotene: the synaptonemal complex dissolves and chiasmata become visible (iii). Diakinesis: terminalisation of chiasmata (i).
solution.why_others_wrong: Nodules cannot appear before synapsis; the synaptonemal complex dissolves only after crossing over; terminalisation of chiasmata is the last event, in diakinesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I: Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option B: (iv) → (ii) → (iii) → (i)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The nucleolus and the nuclear envelope are not seen in a cell at metaphase I.
Reason (R): By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Transition from prophase I to metaphase I
solution.explanation: During diakinesis the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. By the end of diakinesis the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope breaks down; diakinesis represents the transition to metaphase. Hence they are absent at metaphase I, and R explains A.
steps: Lost at the end of diakinesis → absent in the next stage → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I: Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which event occurs in anaphase of mitosis and in anaphase II of meiosis, but NOT in anaphase I of meiosis?

options.text: Reappearance of the nuclear envelope and nucleolus
Splitting of the centromeres and separation of sister chromatids

solution.explanation: In mitotic anaphase, centromeres split and chromatids separate. Anaphase II is similar: the centromere of each chromosome splits and sister chromatids move to opposite poles. In anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.
steps: Mitotic anaphase and anaphase II: centromeres split
Anaphase I: homologues separate, centromeres intact
solution.why_others_wrong: Separation of homologues happens only in anaphase I. Crossing over occurs in pachytene. The nuclear envelope and nucleolus reappear in telophase, not anaphase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Anaphase); Meiosis (Anaphase I; Anaphase II)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Splitting of the centromeres and separation of sister chromatids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (leaf pigment) with List-II (colour on a paper chromatogram).

List-I:
A. Chlorophyll a
B. Chlorophyll b
C. Xanthophylls
D. Carotenoids

List-II:
I. Yellow to yellow-orange
II. Bright or blue green
III. Yellow
IV. Yellow green

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A chromatographic separation of leaf pigments shows chlorophyll a (bright or blue green), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the two chlorophylls, the xanthophylls and carotenoids, or chlorophyll b and xanthophylls.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How Many Types of Pigments are Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The C4 pathway, a cyclic process that operates in plants with Kranz anatomy, has been named the:

solution.explanation: Plants adapted to dry tropical regions have the C4 pathway. This pathway, which has been named the Hatch and Slack pathway, is again a cyclic process.
steps: C4 pathway = Hatch and Slack pathway
solution.why_others_wrong: The EMP pathway is glycolysis and the Krebs cycle is the TCA cycle of respiration. The Z scheme is the pathway of electron transport in the light reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option A: Hatch and Slack pathway

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The light reactions (photochemical phase) include all of the following EXCEPT:

solution.explanation: The light reactions or the 'photochemical' phase include light absorption, water splitting, oxygen release, and the formation of high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH. Fixation of CO₂ into PGA is the carboxylation step of the Calvin cycle, in the biosynthetic phase.
steps: Light reaction: absorption, water splitting, O₂ release, ATP + NADPH
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are all listed by NCERT as parts of the light reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is Light Reaction?
solution.final_answer: Option D: fixation of CO₂ into 3-phosphoglyceric acid

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In non-cyclic photophosphorylation, the two photosystems work in series, first PS II and then PS I.
Statement II: Both ATP and NADPH + H⁺ are synthesised by non-cyclic electron flow.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then PS I, non-cyclic photophosphorylation occurs. The two photosystems are connected through an electron transport chain, and both ATP and NADPH + H⁺ are synthesised by this kind of electron flow.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport (Cyclic and Non-cyclic Photo-phosphorylation)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The CO₂ content of the air is 0.036 per cent by volume. Expressed in microlitres of CO₂ per litre of air (µL L⁻¹), this concentration is (1 L = 10⁶ µL):

solution.concept: CO₂ concentration as a limiting factor
solution.explanation: 0.036 per cent means 0.036 L of CO₂ in 100 L of air, i.e., 0.00036 L per litre. Multiplying by 10⁶ µL per litre gives 360 µL L⁻¹. This is the concentration at which NCERT says C4 plants show saturation, while C3 plants are saturated only beyond 450 µL L⁻¹.
solution.why_others_wrong: 36 and 3600 come from a slip of one power of ten. 0.36 forgets to multiply by 10⁶ for the litre to microlitre conversion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Carbon dioxide Concentration)
solution.final_answer: Option B: 360 µL L⁻¹

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Immediately after light becomes unavailable, the biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis continues for some time and then stops.
Reason (R): The biosynthetic phase does not directly depend on light, but depends on the products of the light reaction, ATP and NADPH.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The biosynthetic phase is not directly light-driven; it uses the ATP and NADPH made in the light reaction. So when light is cut off, it goes on for some time, using up the ATP and NADPH already made, and then stops; when light is given again, synthesis starts again. R explains A.
steps: Runs on stored ATP/NADPH until they are used up → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where are the ATP and NADPH Used?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are internal (plant) factors that affect photosynthesis?

(a) The number, size, age and orientation of leaves
(b) The internal CO₂ concentration
(c) The amount of chlorophyll
(d) The availability of sunlight
(e) Temperature

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The plant (internal) factors include the number, size, age and orientation of leaves, mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, the internal CO₂ concentration and the amount of chlorophyll. The external factors include the availability of sunlight, temperature, CO₂ concentration and water.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes sunlight or temperature, which are external factors.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the Z scheme, the electrons that were moved out of photosystem II must be replaced. They are replaced by electrons:

options.text: returned from photosystem I by cyclic flow
made available by the splitting of water
donated by NADPH formed in the stroma
released when ATP is broken down

solution.explanation: The electrons moved from photosystem II must be replaced; this is achieved by electrons available from the splitting of water, which is associated with PS II. Water is split into 2H⁺, [O] and electrons. The electrons needed to replace those removed from PS I are provided by PS II.
steps: Electrons lost from PS II ← water splitting
Electrons lost from PS I ← PS II
solution.why_others_wrong: Cyclic flow returns electrons to PS I, not PS II. NADPH is the final product that receives electrons, not a donor to PS II. ATP breakdown does not supply electrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Electron Transport (Splitting of Water)
solution.final_answer: Option B: made available by the splitting of water

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Chlorophyll a absorbs maximally in the blue and red regions of the spectrum, and these wavelengths also show a higher rate of photosynthesis.
Statement II: The rate of photosynthesis is highest in the green region of the spectrum, where chlorophyll absorbs most strongly.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The wavelengths at which chlorophyll a absorbs maximally, the blue and red regions, also show a higher rate of photosynthesis; hence chlorophyll a is the chief pigment of photosynthesis. Green light is not where chlorophyll absorbs most strongly, and it does not give the highest rate.
steps: Statement II: false, maximum absorption and rate are in the blue and red regions
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How Many Types of Pigments are Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane is broken down by the movement of protons from the stroma into the lumen through the CF₀ channel.
Statement II: A conformational change in the CF₁ particle of ATP synthase makes the enzyme synthesise ATP.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Protons accumulate in the lumen. The gradient is broken down by the movement of protons across the membrane from the lumen to the stroma through the transmembrane channel of CF₀. This releases enough energy to cause a conformational change in the CF₁ particle of the ATP synthase, which makes the enzyme synthesise ATP.
steps: Statement I: false, protons move from the lumen to the stroma
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are called accessory pigments because they:

options.text: form the reaction centres of both photosystems
also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a

solution.explanation: Though chlorophyll is the major pigment responsible for trapping light, other thylakoid pigments like chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids, called accessory pigments, also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a. This lets a wider range of wavelengths be used.
steps: Accessory pigments: absorb light → pass energy to chlorophyll a
solution.why_others_wrong: The reaction centre of each photosystem is a chlorophyll a molecule. Water splitting is associated with PS II, and CO₂ fixation is done by RuBisCO in the stroma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', How Many Types of Pigments are Involved in Photosynthesis?
solution.final_answer: Option D: also absorb light and transfer the energy to chlorophyll a

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a C3 leaf, ten molecules of RuBP react with RuBisCO: eight combine with CO₂ and two combine with O₂. Each carboxylation gives two molecules of PGA, and each oxygenation gives one molecule of PGA and one of phosphoglycolate. How many molecules of PGA are formed in all?

solution.explanation: Carboxylation: 8 × 2 = 16 PGA. Oxygenation (photorespiration): 2 × 1 = 2 PGA, plus 2 phosphoglycolate. Total PGA = 16 + 2 = 18. Had all ten RuBP been carboxylated, 20 PGA would have formed; photorespiration reduces the yield.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20 treats all ten RuBP as carboxylated. 16 ignores the PGA formed in oxygenation. 14 subtracts the oxygenation products instead of adding them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option C: 18

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cyclic photophosphorylation, which makes ATP but no NADPH, takes place in chloroplasts besides non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Reason (R): The Calvin cycle uses 3 ATP but only 2 NADPH for every CO₂ fixed, and cyclic photophosphorylation probably takes place to meet this difference.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: For every CO₂ molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required. NCERT notes that it is probably to meet this difference in the numbers of ATP and NADPH used in the dark reaction that cyclic phosphorylation takes place. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Extra ATP need → cyclic flow → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Even though water is one of the reactants in the light reaction, its effect as a factor is more through its effect on the plant than directly on photosynthesis.
Statement II: C3 plants have a much higher temperature optimum for photosynthesis than C4 plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the effect of water as a factor is more through its effect on the plant (stomatal closure, wilting) than directly on photosynthesis. C4 plants respond to higher temperatures and show a higher rate of photosynthesis, while C3 plants have a much lower temperature optimum.
steps: Statement II: false, C3 plants have the lower temperature optimum
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Temperature; Water)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Within the chloroplast, the membrane system is responsible for trapping light energy and for the synthesis of ATP and NADPH.
(b) RuBisCO is named RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase because its active site can bind both CO₂ and O₂.
(c) While discussing light as a factor, light quality, light intensity and the duration of exposure to light have to be distinguished.
(d) When light is abundant, the rate of photosynthesis is decided by light alone, and other factors have no effect.
(e) Photosynthesis takes place in all parts of the plant, including the roots.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Site, enzyme and factors of photosynthesis
solution.explanation: In the chloroplast, the membrane system traps light energy and synthesises ATP and NADPH, while the stroma holds the enzymes that make sugar. RuBisCO is RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase; its active site binds both CO₂ and O₂. Light quality, intensity and duration must be distinguished. Photosynthesis is affected by several factors simultaneously, and the rate is set by the factor nearest its minimal value. It takes place only in the green parts of the plant, mostly the leaves.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (d) or (e), which are false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis take place?; Photorespiration; Factors affecting Photosynthesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: ATP is called the energy currency of the cell because:

options.text: the energy of respiration is used directly by the cell without being stored in any molecule
ATP is the main respiratory substrate oxidised in the mitochondria
ATP stores the energy of glucose permanently and is never broken down
the energy released by oxidation in respiration is used to synthesise ATP, which is broken down whenever and wherever energy needs to be utilised

solution.explanation: The energy released by oxidation in respiration is not (or rather cannot be) used directly; it is used to synthesise ATP, which is broken down whenever and wherever energy needs to be utilised. Hence ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell.
steps: ATP broken down where energy is needed → energy currency
solution.why_others_wrong: The energy of respiration cannot be used directly. The respiratory substrates are carbohydrates and, under some conditions, fats, proteins and organic acids, not ATP. ATP is broken down whenever energy is needed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Introduction
solution.final_answer: Option D: the energy released by oxidation in respiration is used to synthesise ATP, which is broken down whenever and wherever energy needs to be utilised

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plants have no specialised organs for gaseous exchange. For this purpose they have:

solution.explanation: Plants, unlike animals, have no specialised organs for gaseous exchange, but they have stomata and lenticels for this purpose.
solution.why_others_wrong: Lungs, air sacs and gills are animal organs. Root hairs absorb water and minerals; they are not the structures NCERT names for gaseous exchange.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Do Plants Breathe?
solution.final_answer: Option B: stomata and lenticels

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The term glycolysis has originated from two Greek words, which mean:

solution.explanation: The term glycolysis has originated from the Greek words glycos, for sugar, and lysis, for splitting.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other pairs do not match the Greek roots glycos and lysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option B: sugar and splitting

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In glycolysis, a chain of ten reactions, under the control of different enzymes, takes place to produce pyruvate from glucose.
Statement II: Pyruvic acid is the key product of glycolysis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In glycolysis, a chain of ten reactions under the control of different enzymes produces pyruvate from glucose. Pyruvic acid is the key product of glycolysis; its metabolic fate depends on the cellular need.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Germinating seeds in a respirometer consume 50 mL of O₂ and give out 35 mL of CO₂ in the same time. What is the respiratory quotient (RQ), and which type of respiratory substrate is mainly being used?

solution.explanation: RQ = volume of CO₂ evolved ÷ volume of O₂ consumed = 35 ÷ 50 = 0.7. For carbohydrates completely oxidised, RQ = 1; for fats RQ is less than 1 (tripalmitin gives about 0.7). An RQ of 0.7 therefore points to fat as the substrate.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.43 inverts the ratio (O₂ ÷ CO₂). A carbohydrate gives an RQ of 1, not 0.7. 1.0 does not follow from the volumes given.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Respiratory Quotient
solution.final_answer: Option B: 0.7; fat

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plants do not present great demands for gas exchange.
Reason (R): Roots, stems and leaves respire at rates far lower than animals do.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why plants need no respiratory organs
solution.explanation: NCERT gives three reasons why plants can get along without respiratory organs. The second is that plants do not present great demands for gas exchange, because roots, stems and leaves respire at rates far lower than animals do; only during photosynthesis are large volumes of gases exchanged. R explains A.
steps: Low respiratory rate → low demand for gas exchange → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Do Plants Breathe?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the fate of pyruvic acid are correct?

(a) The three major ways in which cells handle pyruvic acid are lactic acid fermentation, alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration.
(b) Fermentation takes place under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes.
(c) Some bacteria produce lactic acid from pyruvic acid.
(d) In fermentation, glucose is completely degraded to CO₂ and H₂O.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Pyruvic acid formed in glycolysis is handled in three major ways: lactic acid fermentation, alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration. Fermentation occurs under anaerobic conditions in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes; some bacteria produce lactic acid from pyruvic acid. Fermentation accounts for only a partial breakdown of glucose; complete degradation to CO₂ and H₂O happens in aerobic respiration.
steps: (d) false: fermentation is a partial breakdown
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes the false statement (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (enzyme or complex) with List-II (role).

List-I:
A. Citrate synthase
B. NADH dehydrogenase (complex I)
C. Cytochrome bc₁ complex (complex III)
D. F₁ headpiece of ATP synthase

List-II:
I. Contains the site for the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate
II. Transfers electrons from reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) to cytochrome c
III. Condenses the acetyl group with oxaloacetic acid and water to form citric acid
IV. Oxidises NADH and passes the electrons to ubiquinone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The TCA cycle starts with the condensation of the acetyl group with OAA and water to give citric acid, catalysed by citrate synthase. In the ETS, NADH dehydrogenase (complex I) oxidises NADH and transfers the electrons to ubiquinone. Reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is oxidised with the transfer of electrons to cytochrome c via the cytochrome bc₁ complex (complex III). The F₁ headpiece of ATP synthase is a peripheral membrane protein complex that contains the site for ATP synthesis.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap citrate synthase with complex I, complex I with complex III, or complex III with the F₁ headpiece.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle; Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Glycerol enters the respiratory pathway after being converted to PGAL.
Statement II: Fatty acids enter the respiratory pathway after being converted to pyruvic acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Fats are first broken down into glycerol and fatty acids. Glycerol enters the pathway after being converted to PGAL (3-phosphoglyceraldehyde). Fatty acids are degraded to acetyl CoA and enter the pathway at that point, not as pyruvic acid.
steps: Statement II: false, fatty acids enter as acetyl CoA
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Amphibolic Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Use the assumptions of the respiratory balance sheet: complete oxidation of one glucose gives 10 NADH and 2 FADH₂ in all; every NADH (including that of glycolysis) is oxidised in the ETS, giving 3 ATP, and every FADH₂ gives 2 ATP; and 2 H⁺ pass through F₀ for each ATP made by ATP synthase. The remaining ATP (net 2 in glycolysis and 2 from GTP in the TCA cycle) is made directly. How many protons pass through F₀ for the oxidation of one glucose?

solution.explanation: ATP made by ATP synthase (oxidative phosphorylation) = 10 × 3 + 2 × 2 = 34. The other 4 of the 38 ATP are made directly in glycolysis and the TCA cycle and need no proton flow. Protons through F₀ = 34 × 2 = 68.
solution.why_others_wrong: 76 counts all 38 ATP as made by ATP synthase. 60 counts only the ATP from NADH. 72 removes only the 2 ATP formed via GTP and forgets the net 2 ATP made directly in glycolysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation; The Respiratory Balance Sheet
solution.final_answer: Option D: 68

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the electron transport system are correct?

(a) The number of ATP molecules synthesised depends on the nature of the electron donor.
(b) The electron transport system is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
(c) As electrons pass from complex I to complex IV, the flow is coupled to ATP synthase (complex V) for the production of ATP.
(d) Complex IV transfers electrons to ubiquinone.
(e) Oxygen is the first acceptor of the electrons removed from NADH.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The ETS is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Electrons from NADH pass to ubiquinone via complex I, then through complex III and cytochrome c to complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), and finally to oxygen, the final acceptor. Their passage from complex I to IV is coupled to ATP synthase (complex V). The number of ATP molecules synthesised depends on the nature of the electron donor: 3 per NADH and 2 per FADH₂.
steps: (d) false: complex I passes electrons to ubiquinone
(e) false: oxygen is the final acceptor
solution.why_others_wrong: Every wrong option includes (d) or (e), which are false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cells oxidise glucose not in one step but in several small steps.
Reason (R): In stepwise oxidation, some steps release just enough energy to be coupled to ATP synthesis, so not all the liberated energy goes out as heat.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: If glucose were burnt in one step, as in complete combustion, most of the energy would be given out as heat and could not be trapped. Plant cells catabolise glucose in several small steps, some just large enough for the released energy to be coupled to ATP synthesis. R explains why cells use the stepwise route.
steps: Stepwise release lets energy be trapped as ATP → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Introduction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Two molecules of NADH are produced when the two molecules of pyruvic acid formed from one glucose are converted to acetyl CoA.
Statement II: Two molecules of FADH₂ are produced when the two molecules of pyruvic acid formed from one glucose are converted to acetyl CoA.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Pyruvate entering the mitochondrial matrix undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by pyruvic dehydrogenase, with NAD⁺ and coenzyme A. During this process two molecules of NADH are produced from the two molecules of pyruvic acid derived from one glucose. FADH₂ is not formed here; it is formed in the TCA cycle (one per acetyl CoA).
steps: Statement II: false, FADH₂ is formed in the TCA cycle, not in the link reaction
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about plant growth regulators (PGRs) are correct?

(a) PGRs are also variously described as plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones.
(b) Growth promoters are involved in activities such as cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting and seed formation.
(c) Growth-inhibiting PGRs play an important role in plant responses to wounds and to stresses of biotic and abiotic origin, and in dormancy and abscission.
(d) Abscisic acid belongs to the group of plant growth promoters.
(e) Auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins belong to the group of plant growth inhibitors.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PGRs are small, simple molecules of diverse chemical composition, also called plant growth substances, plant hormones or phytohormones. One group promotes growth (cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting, seed formation): auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins. The other group acts in responses to wounds and stresses and in growth-inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission: abscisic acid belongs here.
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (d) or (e), which swap the promoter and inhibitor groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: characteristics
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Meristematic phase
B. Phase of elongation
C. Phase of maturation
D. Redifferentiation

List-II:
I. Cells attain their maximal size in terms of wall thickening and protoplasmic modifications
II. Cells derived from a dedifferentiated meristem again lose the capacity to divide and mature to perform specific functions
III. Cells are rich in protoplasm, with large conspicuous nuclei and thin, primary, cellulosic walls having abundant plasmodesmatal connections
IV. Cells show increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new cell wall deposition

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The constantly dividing cells at the root and shoot apex form the meristematic phase: rich protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary cellulosic walls with abundant plasmodesmata. Cells just behind it are in the phase of elongation (vacuolation, enlargement, new wall deposition). Further away lies the phase of maturation, where cells reach their maximal size in wall thickening and protoplasmic modification. Cells produced by a dedifferentiated meristem that again lose the capacity to divide are redifferentiated.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps the meristematic and elongation descriptions; option B swaps elongation and maturation; option C swaps maturation and redifferentiation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', phases of growth; differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Plants follow different pathways in response to the environment or to phases of life, and so form different kinds of structures; heterophylly is an example. This ability of plants is called:

solution.explanation: NCERT defines plasticity as the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to the environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. Heterophylly (different leaf shapes in juvenile and mature plants, or in air and water) is the standard example.
steps: Different structures in response to environment/phase of life → plasticity
solution.why_others_wrong: Dedifferentiation is the regaining of the capacity to divide; apical dominance is the inhibition of lateral buds by the apical bud; senescence is ageing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', development: plasticity
solution.final_answer: Option B: Plasticity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which plant growth regulator acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism?

solution.concept: Abscisic acid as a growth inhibitor
solution.explanation: NCERT states that ABA acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. It also inhibits seed germination and stimulates the closure of stomata.
steps: General growth inhibitor + metabolic inhibitor → abscisic acid
solution.why_others_wrong: Gibberellic acid, zeatin (a cytokinin) and IAA (an auxin) are all plant growth promoters.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Growth and Development', plant growth regulators: abscisic acid
solution.final_answer: Option C: Abscisic acid

questions.subject: Botany
