questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: The haploid human genome has approximately 3 × 10⁹ bp. If the cost of sequencing was US $3 per bp (the estimated cost at the beginning of the Human Genome Project), the approximate total cost of sequencing would be:

solution.concept: Scale of the Human Genome Project
solution.explanation: Cost = number of base pairs × cost per base pair = 3 × 10⁹ × 3 = 9 × 10⁹ US dollars, i.e. about 9 billion US dollars, the figure NCERT gives to show the enormity of the project.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 billion forgets to multiply by the cost per bp; 1 billion divides instead of multiplying; 18 billion counts both copies of a diploid genome, but the estimate is for the 3 × 10⁹ bp genome.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project
solution.final_answer: Option B: 9 billion US dollars

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The split-gene arrangement probably represents an ancient feature of the genome; the presence of introns is reminiscent of antiquity, and splicing represents the dominance of the RNA world.
Statement II: Split genes are typical of bacterial genes, and introns are absent from eukaryotic genes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that split-gene arrangements probably represent an ancient feature of the genome, that introns are reminiscent of antiquity and that splicing represents the dominance of the RNA world; Statement I is true. Split genes, with exons interrupted by introns, are a feature of eukaryotes; bacterial genes are not split. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, split genes are eukaryotic
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): DNA-dependent DNA polymerases must catalyse polymerisation not only fast but also with a high degree of accuracy.
Reason (R): Errors made during DNA replication never lead to mutations.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: DNA polymerases have to polymerise a large number of nucleotides in a very short time and with high accuracy, so A is true. NCERT notes that any mistake during replication would result in mutations, so R is false.
steps: R: false, replication errors result in mutations
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In its inactive state, the ribosome exists as a single, undivided particle.
Statement II: The translation of an mRNA into protein begins when the small subunit of the ribosome encounters the mRNA.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The ribosome is the cellular factory for protein synthesis. In its inactive state it exists as two subunits, a large and a small one, so Statement I is false. When the small subunit encounters an mRNA, the process of translation begins. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, two separate subunits
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', translation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about DNA fingerprinting are correct?

(a) DNA from every tissue of an individual, such as blood, hair follicle, skin, bone, saliva or sperm, shows the same degree of polymorphism.
(b) The band pattern obtained differs from individual to individual in a population, except in monozygotic (identical) twins.
(c) The VNTR used as a probe belongs to a class of satellite DNA referred to as mini-satellite.
(d) The use of PCR has reduced the sensitivity of the technique, so large amounts of tissue are now needed.
(e) DNA fingerprinting is based on differences in the protein-coding sequences, which make up most of the human genome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: DNA from any tissue of an individual shows the same polymorphism, which is why blood, hair follicles, saliva or sperm can be used. The VNTR probe is a mini-satellite; VNTR sizes vary, giving bands that differ between individuals except monozygotic twins. PCR has increased the sensitivity, so DNA from a single cell is enough. Fingerprinting uses repetitive (satellite) DNA, and less than 2 per cent of the genome codes for proteins.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: E. coli grown for many generations in a ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium is transferred to a ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium. E. coli divides once every 20 minutes and DNA replicates semiconservatively. After 80 minutes, what fractions of the DNA molecules are hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N) and light (¹⁴N/¹⁴N)?

solution.explanation: 80 minutes = 4 generations, so one ¹⁵N molecule becomes 2⁴ = 16 molecules. The two original heavy strands are never lost; each ends up in one hybrid molecule. So 2 of 16 molecules (1/8) are hybrid and the remaining 14 (7/8) are light.
solution.shortcut: After n generations, hybrid = 2/2ⁿ; light = 1 − 2/2ⁿ.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/4 hybrid is the result after 60 minutes (3 generations); 1/2 after 40 minutes (2 generations); 1/16 counts only one hybrid molecule instead of two.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: 1/8 hybrid and 7/8 light

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements related to the methods and findings of the Human Genome Project are correct?

(a) Sequence annotation is the approach of sequencing the whole genome, coding and non-coding, and later assigning functions to different regions of the sequence.
(b) The genome sequences of several non-human model organisms, such as bacteria, yeast, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila, rice and Arabidopsis, have also been determined.
(c) Repetitive sequences are thought to have no direct coding functions, but they shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution.
(d) Repetitive sequences make up less than 2 per cent of the human genome and code for most proteins.
(e) The commonly used hosts for cloning DNA fragments in the project were mammalian cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Methodologies and findings of the HGP
solution.explanation: Sequence annotation sequences the whole genome and later assigns functions; ESTs instead identify expressed genes. Genomes of model organisms such as bacteria, yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila, rice and Arabidopsis have also been sequenced. Repetitive sequences, repeated hundreds to thousands of times, make up a large portion of the genome, have no direct coding function, but shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution. DNA fragments were cloned in bacteria and yeast using BAC and YAC vectors.
steps: (d): false, repeats are a large, non-coding part
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: methodologies; salient features
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A mutant E. coli has an altered i gene whose product (the repressor) can no longer bind to the operator. What happens to the structural genes of the lac operon in this mutant when lactose is absent?

options.text: The z, y and a genes stay switched off until lactose is supplied
The z, y and a genes are transcribed even though lactose is absent
Only the i gene is transcribed; the structural genes stay silent
The structural genes are transcribed but cannot be translated in the absence of lactose

solution.concept: Negative regulation of the lac operon
solution.explanation: Normally, in the absence of an inducer, the repressor binds the operator and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. If the repressor cannot bind the operator, nothing blocks RNA polymerase, so the structural genes z, y and a are transcribed all the time, whether or not lactose is present.
steps: Operon is switched off only by repressor bound to operator
No binding → no block → continuous transcription
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactose acts only by inactivating the repressor, and here the repressor is already unable to act. The mRNA of the operon needs no lactose to be translated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option B: The z, y and a genes are transcribed even though lactose is absent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The length of the DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is about 2.2 metres, far greater than the dimension of a typical nucleus (about 10⁻⁶ m).
Statement II: In eukaryotes, chromatin fibres are further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT multiplies 6.6 × 10⁹ bp by 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m per bp to get about 2.2 m of DNA, which must fit into a nucleus of about 10⁻⁶ m; hence the need for packaging. Nucleosomes form the chromatin fibre, which is further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The genetic code is nearly universal; for example, from bacteria to humans UUU codes for phenylalanine.
Reason (R): AUG has dual functions: it codes for methionine and also acts as the initiator codon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Universality of the code and the initiator codon
solution.explanation: Both statements are features of the genetic code listed by NCERT. The near-universality of the code (with some exceptions in mitochondrial codons and some protozoans) is a separate feature from the dual role of AUG. R does not explain why UUU means phenylalanine in all these organisms.
steps: Different features of the code → R does not explain A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If one strand of a DNA segment reads 5'-ATGC-3', its complementary strand, also written in the 5'→3' direction, reads 5'-GCAT-3'.
Reason (R): In double-stranded DNA, the two polynucleotide chains run in the same direction (parallel polarity).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Base pairing gives the complement 3'-TACG-5' opposite 5'-ATGC-3'. Written 5'→3', this is 5'-GCAT-3', so A is true. This works only because the two chains have antiparallel polarity (one 5'→3', the other 3'→5'); R says they are parallel and is false.
steps: R: false, the chains are antiparallel
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain: double helix
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a biogas plant, the biogas produced from a slurry of cattle dung is supplied through an outlet pipe to nearby houses. NCERT states that it is used for:

solution.explanation: A biogas plant has a concrete tank in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed; a floating cover rises as microbial activity produces gas. An outlet pipe carries the gas to nearby houses, where the biogas is used for cooking and lighting.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statins come from the fungus Monascus purpureus, fruit juices are clarified with pectinases and proteases, and Swiss cheese is ripened by Propionibacterium sharmanii; none uses biogas.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas
solution.final_answer: Option C: Cooking and lighting

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The ladybird beetle (with red and black markings) and dragonflies are useful biocontrol agents. They help to get rid of, respectively:

solution.explanation: NCERT gives the Ladybird beetle and dragonflies as familiar examples of biological control: the Ladybird is useful to get rid of aphids and dragonflies to get rid of mosquitoes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B reverses the pair. Butterfly caterpillars are controlled by Bacillus thuringiensis, and fungal pathogens by Trichoderma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option A: Aphids and mosquitoes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the main sources of biofertilisers are:

solution.explanation: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil. The main sources are bacteria (e.g. Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum), fungi (mycorrhiza-forming Glomus) and cyanobacteria (Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria).
solution.why_others_wrong: Urea and phosphate salts are chemical fertilisers; insects, nematodes, viruses and protozoa are not the sources NCERT lists.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: Bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In paddy fields, cyanobacteria are weeds that reduce soil fertility.
Statement II: Plants having mycorrhizal associations show resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought, and an overall increase in plant growth and development.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Cyanobacteria are autotrophic microbes, many of which fix atmospheric nitrogen; in paddy fields they serve as an important biofertiliser and also add organic matter, increasing fertility. Statement I is false. Besides helping in phosphorus absorption, mycorrhiza (e.g. Glomus) gives the plant resistance to root-borne pathogens, tolerance to salinity and drought and better overall growth. Statement II is true.
steps: Statement I: false, cyanobacteria are an important biofertiliser in paddy
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In secondary treatment, the primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it.
Reason (R): Agitation and aeration promote the growth of anaerobic methanogens, which form flocs in the aeration tank.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A is NCERT's description of the aeration tank. The purpose is to allow vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs (bacteria associated with fungal filaments), which consume the organic matter and reduce the BOD. Methanogens are anaerobic and act later, in the anaerobic sludge digesters. R is false.
steps: R: false, aeration favours aerobic flocs; methanogens work in anaerobic digesters
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment: secondary treatment
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Microbes are also used to ferment fish, soybean and bamboo shoots to make foods.
Statement II: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, commonly called brewer's yeast, is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices to produce citric acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that microbes are used to ferment fish, soybean and bamboo shoots to make foods; Statement I is true. Saccharomyces cerevisiae (brewer's yeast) ferments malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol, not citric acid; citric acid is produced by the fungus Aspergillus niger. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, the product is ethanol
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products; fermented beverages
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) as a biocontrol agent are correct?

(a) It is available in sachets as dried spores, which are mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants.
(b) When the insect larvae eat the sprayed spores, the toxin is released in their gut and the larvae are killed.
(c) The bacterial disease kills the caterpillars but leaves other insects unharmed.
(d) Its toxin genes have been introduced into plants, such as Bt cotton, making them resistant to insect pests.
(e) Bt is a fungus that is used mainly to kill weeds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Bt spores are sold as dried spores in sachets, mixed with water and sprayed on plants such as brassicas and fruit trees. Insect larvae eat them; the toxin is released in the gut and kills the larvae. The disease kills the caterpillars but leaves other insects unharmed. Using genetic engineering, Bt toxin genes have been put into plants (Bt cotton) to make them resistant to insect pests. Bt is a bacterium, and it controls insects, not weeds.
steps: (e): false, Bt is a bacterium acting on insects
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D include (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (step in municipal sewage treatment) with List-II (what happens).

List-I:
A. Sequential filtration in primary treatment
B. Sedimentation in primary treatment
C. Settling tank after the aeration tank
D. Effluent from secondary treatment

List-II:
I. Generally released into natural water bodies such as rivers and streams
II. Removal of grit (soil and small pebbles)
III. Removal of floating debris
IV. Bacterial flocs sediment to form activated sludge

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In primary treatment, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration and then grit (soil and small pebbles) by sedimentation; the settled solids form the primary sludge and the supernatant is the primary effluent. After the aeration tanks, the effluent passes to a settling tank where the bacterial flocs sediment as activated sludge. The effluent from secondary treatment is generally released into natural water bodies such as rivers and streams.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B swaps filtration and sedimentation; option C swaps the settling tank and the final effluent; option D places grit removal in the settling tank.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A small amount of curd added to fresh milk as an inoculum or starter converts the milk into curd.
Reason (R): The starter contains millions of lactic acid bacteria, which multiply at suitable temperatures and convert the milk to curd.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: a small amount of curd added to fresh milk as inoculum or starter contains millions of LAB, which at suitable temperatures multiply, thus converting milk to curd (LAB produce acids that coagulate and partially digest the milk proteins). R explains A.
steps: The LAB in the starter are what convert the milk
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements reflect the approach of organic farming and biological control described in NCERT?

(a) A key belief of the organic farmer is that biodiversity furthers health.
(b) The more variety a landscape has, the more sustainable it is.
(c) Becoming familiar with the life forms in the field, predators and pests, their life cycles, patterns of feeding and preferred habitats, helps develop appropriate means of biocontrol.
(d) The use of biocontrol measures increases our dependence on toxic chemicals and pesticides.
(e) Chemical pesticides kill only harmful insects and spare the useful ones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The organic farmer believes that biodiversity furthers health and that the more variety a landscape has, the more sustainable it is. Knowing the life forms of the field, predators as well as pests, with their life cycles, feeding patterns and habitats, helps develop appropriate biocontrol. Biocontrol reduces dependence on toxic chemicals, which kill useful and harmful organisms alike and pollute soil, ground water and crops.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: An age pyramid in which the pre-reproductive and reproductive age groups are nearly equal, giving a bell shape, represents a population that is:

solution.explanation: Age pyramids show the proportions of pre-reproductive, reproductive and post-reproductive individuals. A triangular pyramid with a broad base indicates an expanding population, a bell-shaped one a stable population and an urn-shaped one a declining population.
solution.why_others_wrong: Expanding populations give a broad-based triangular pyramid and declining ones an urn shape; NCERT does not link any shape to extinction within a generation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Stable

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT illustrates that population size can vary enormously, from fewer than 10 individuals to millions. Which pair does it use as examples of these two extremes?

options.text: Tigers in a national park; Parthenium plants in a field
Siberian cranes at the Bharatpur wetlands in any year; Chlamydomonas in a pond
Banyan trees in a village; fish in a lake
Elephants in a forest; fruit flies in a laboratory culture

solution.explanation: NCERT: the size of a population could be as low as fewer than 10 (Siberian cranes at Bharatpur wetlands in any year) or go into millions (Chlamydomonas in a pond). Population size, technically called population density (N), is not a static parameter.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other pairs mix organisms NCERT uses for other points (tiger census, percent cover of a banyan, the elephant in exponential growth), not as the extremes of population size.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Siberian cranes at the Bharatpur wetlands in any year; Chlamydomonas in a pond

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In interference competition between two species:

options.text: Both species benefit from sharing the same food
One species benefits and the other is unaffected
Competition occurs only when food and space are in short supply
The feeding efficiency of one species is reduced by the interfering and inhibitory presence of the other, even if resources are abundant

solution.explanation: Competition is usually thought to occur when species compete for the same limiting resources. But NCERT notes that in interference competition, the feeding efficiency of one species might be reduced due to the interfering and inhibitory presence of the other species, even if resources (food and space) are abundant.
steps: Interference competition can occur even with abundant resources
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A describes mutualism and option B commensalism; option C is exactly what interference competition contradicts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: competition
solution.final_answer: Option D: The feeding efficiency of one species is reduced by the interfering and inhibitory presence of the other, even if resources are abundant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: To show that any species growing exponentially under unlimited resources can reach enormous population densities in a short time, Darwin used the example of a slow-growing animal. That animal was the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: any species growing exponentially under unlimited resource conditions can reach enormous population densities in a short time. Darwin showed how even a slow-growing animal like the elephant could reach enormous numbers in the absence of checks.
steps: Even the slow-breeding elephant → enormous numbers without checks
solution.why_others_wrong: Fruit flies, flour beetles and Norway rats are fast breeders, so they would not make Darwin's point about a slow-growing animal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth
solution.final_answer: Option A: Elephant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the absence of predators, prey populations would always decline because they lose their source of food.
Statement II: Interspecific interactions arise from the interaction of populations of the same species.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: predators keep prey populations under control; but for predators, prey species could achieve very high population densities and cause ecosystem instability. Predators are not the food of their prey, so Statement I is false. Interspecific interactions arise from the interaction of populations of two different species, so Statement II is also false.
steps: Statement I: false, prey could reach very high densities
Statement II: false, two different species
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Many marine fish are infested with ectoparasitic copepods.
Statement II: The life cycles of endoparasites are simpler than those of ectoparasites, because endoparasites live in a protected environment.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Ectoparasites feed on the external surface of the host: lice on humans, ticks on dogs and copepods on many marine fish; Statement I is true. Endoparasites live inside the host body at different sites (liver, kidney, lungs, red blood cells); NCERT states that their life cycles are more complex because of their extreme specialisation. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, endoparasite life cycles are more complex
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they become invasive and start spreading fast.
Reason (R): Predators act as conduits for energy transfer across trophic levels.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Invasive species and the roles of predators
solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements. Exotic species become invasive because the invaded land does not have their natural predators (as with the prickly pear cactus in Australia). R describes a different role of predators, transferring energy across trophic levels, and does not explain why exotics spread.
steps: A: true (no natural predators in the new land)
R is a different role of predators
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In nature, plants rarely need the help of animals for pollinating their flowers or dispersing their seeds.
Reason (R): Plants offer rewards or 'fees' to animals in the form of pollen and nectar for pollinators and juicy and nutritious fruits for seed dispersers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: plants need the help of animals for pollinating their flowers and dispersing their seeds, so A is false. Animals have to be 'paid' for these services: plants offer pollen and nectar to pollinators and juicy, nutritious fruits to seed dispersers. R is true.
steps: A: false, plants commonly depend on animals for pollination and dispersal
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: mutualism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Population density must always be expressed as the number of individuals.
Statement II: The total number of individuals in a population is always easy to determine and is never meaningless as a measure of population size.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: population size, technically called population density (N), need not necessarily be measured in numbers only; percent cover or biomass may be used. Although the total number is generally the most appropriate measure, it is in some cases either meaningless or difficult to determine. Both statements are false.
steps: Statement I: false, cover or biomass may be used
Statement II: false, sometimes meaningless or difficult
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population attributes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Two species competing for the same resource could avoid competition by choosing, for instance, different times for feeding or different foraging patterns.
Statement II: A species whose distribution is restricted to a small geographical area because of a competitively superior species is found to expand its distributional range dramatically when the competing species is experimentally removed; this is called competitive release.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that species facing competition might evolve mechanisms that promote co-existence rather than exclusion, such as resource partitioning: different feeding times or foraging patterns. It also cites competitive release, the dramatic range expansion of a restricted species when its superior competitor is removed, as evidence that competition occurs in nature. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: competition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A population of 250 individuals grows exponentially according to Nₜ = N₀e^(rt), with r = 0.0231 per year. Taking ln 2 = 0.693, what will the population size be after 60 years?

solution.explanation: rt = 0.0231 × 60 = 1.386 = 2 × 0.693 = 2 ln 2. So e^(rt) = e^(2 ln 2) = 2² = 4, and Nₜ = 250 × 4 = 1000. The population doubles every 0.693/0.0231 = 30 years, i.e. twice in 60 years.
solution.shortcut: Doubling time = ln 2 / r = 30 years; 60 years = 2 doublings.
solution.why_others_wrong: 500 counts only one doubling; 597 treats growth as linear, 250 × (1 + rt); 2000 counts three doublings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth
solution.final_answer: Option D: 1000

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about parasitism are correct?

(a) Parasites may reduce the survival, growth and reproduction of the host and reduce its population density.
(b) Parasites might render the host more vulnerable to predation by making it physically weak.
(c) Brood parasitism is shown by Cuscuta growing on hedge plants.
(d) Endoparasites have elaborate morphological and anatomical features and a low reproductive potential.
(e) The eggs of a brood-parasitic bird have evolved to resemble the host's eggs in size and colour.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Parasites may reduce host survival, growth, reproduction and population density, and can make the host physically weak and more vulnerable to predation. In brood parasitism (e.g. the cuckoo laying eggs in the crow's nest) the parasite's eggs resemble the host's in size and colour, reducing the chance of detection. Cuscuta is a parasitic plant, not a brood parasite. Endoparasites have greatly simplified morphological and anatomical features while emphasising their reproductive potential.
steps: (c): false, Cuscuta is a plant parasite
(d): false, features simplified, high reproductive potential
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, C and D include (c) or (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Considering the effect of each interspecific interaction on the two species involved, in which pair of interactions does neither species benefit?

solution.explanation: Mutualism (+, +) benefits both; predation and parasitism (+, −) benefit one species; commensalism (+, 0) benefits one. In competition (−, −) both lose, and in amensalism (−, 0) one is harmed and the other unaffected, so neither species benefits in these two.
steps: All others have at least one +
solution.why_others_wrong: Predation, parasitism and commensalism each benefit one species, and mutualism benefits both.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Competition and amensalism

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following may be considered a man-made ecosystem?

solution.explanation: Ecosystems are broadly terrestrial (forest, grassland, desert) or aquatic (pond, lake, wetland, river, estuary). NCERT adds that crop fields and an aquarium may also be considered man-made ecosystems.
solution.why_others_wrong: Grasslands and deserts are natural terrestrial ecosystems; an estuary is a natural aquatic ecosystem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function
solution.final_answer: Option B: An aquarium

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The common herbivores (primary consumers) of an aquatic ecosystem, according to NCERT, are:

options.text: Fishes that feed on other fishes

solution.explanation: Animals that feed on producers are primary consumers (herbivores). NCERT names insects, birds and mammals as the common herbivores of terrestrial ecosystems and molluscs in aquatic ecosystems.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mammals are listed as terrestrial herbivores; fish-eating fishes are carnivores; fungi and bacteria are decomposers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option B: Molluscs

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The three ecological pyramids that are usually studied are the pyramids of:

solution.explanation: In an ecological pyramid the base is formed by the producers (first trophic level) and the apex by the top-level consumers. The three pyramids usually studied are the pyramid of number, the pyramid of biomass and the pyramid of energy.
steps: Pyramids of number, biomass and energy
solution.why_others_wrong: Area, age, sex ratio and natality are population attributes or measures, and productivity and decomposition are ecosystem functions, not types of pyramid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option A: Number, biomass and energy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The natural interconnection of food chains in an ecosystem makes a:

solution.explanation: In nature, food chains do not run in isolation. NCERT: the natural interconnection of food chains makes it a food web.
solution.why_others_wrong: A trophic level is a specific place in a food chain; standing crop is the biomass at a trophic level; an ecological pyramid represents the food or energy relationship between levels.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option C: Food web

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require.
Reason (R): Ecosystems are not exempt from the second law of thermodynamics, and the energy supply counteracts the universal tendency towards increasing disorderliness.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Energy flow and the second law of thermodynamics
solution.explanation: NCERT: ecosystems are not exempt from the second law of thermodynamics. They need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require, to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Second law → constant energy input needed → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Decomposition is quicker if the detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances such as sugars.
Reason (R): Temperature and soil moisture have no influence on the rate of decomposition.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The rate of decomposition is controlled by the chemical composition of the detritus and by climatic factors. Decomposition is quicker if the detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars, and slower if it is rich in lignin and chitin, so A is true. Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on soil microbes, so R is false.
steps: R: false, temperature and moisture are the key climatic regulators
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Primary production is expressed in terms of weight (g m⁻²) or energy (kcal m⁻²).
Statement II: The rate of biomass production is called the standing crop.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis, expressed as weight (g m⁻²) or energy (kcal m⁻²); Statement I is true. The rate of biomass production is called productivity. Standing crop is the mass of living material at a trophic level at a particular time, a quantity rather than a rate. Statement II is false.
steps: Statement II: false, the rate is productivity
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a pyramid of energy, each bar indicates:

options.text: The number of species present at each trophic level
The dry weight of a single individual of each trophic level
The energy lost as heat by the whole ecosystem in a year
The amount of energy present at each trophic level in a given time, or annually, per unit area

solution.explanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright, because some energy is lost as heat at each transfer. NCERT states that each bar in the energy pyramid indicates the amount of energy present at each trophic level in a given time or annually per unit area.
steps: Each bar = energy at that trophic level per unit area per unit time
solution.why_others_wrong: Pyramids deal with individuals, biomass or energy at a trophic level, not the number of species; biomass pyramids use all organisms, not a single individual; heat loss is not what the bars show.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option D: The amount of energy present at each trophic level in a given time, or annually, per unit area

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (organism in the food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake) with List-II (position in the food chain).

List-I:
A. Grasshopper
B. Frog
C. Snake
D. Grass

List-II:
I. Primary carnivore (secondary consumer), third trophic level
II. Producer, first trophic level
III. Herbivore (primary consumer), second trophic level
IV. Secondary carnivore (tertiary consumer), fourth trophic level

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Trophic levels in a grazing food chain
solution.explanation: Producers (grass) form the first trophic level. Herbivores (grasshopper) are primary consumers at the second level. Consumers that eat herbivores (frog) are primary carnivores, i.e. secondary consumers, at the third level. Those that eat primary carnivores (snake) are secondary carnivores, i.e. tertiary consumers, at the fourth level.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps grasshopper and frog; option C swaps frog and snake; option D swaps grass and grasshopper.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow: trophic levels
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A field receives 10,00,000 kJ of incident solar radiation. Assume that 40 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), that the plants fix 2 per cent of the PAR as gross primary productivity (GPP), and that the plants use 30 per cent of their GPP in respiration. What is the net primary productivity (NPP)?

solution.concept: From incident radiation to net primary productivity
solution.explanation: PAR = 40% of 10,00,000 = 4,00,000 kJ. GPP = 2% of PAR = 8,000 kJ. Respiration = 30% of GPP = 2,400 kJ. NPP = GPP − respiration = 8,000 − 2,400 = 5,600 kJ. (NCERT: less than 50 per cent of incident radiation is PAR, and plants capture only 2–10 per cent of the PAR.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 8,000 kJ is the GPP (respiration not subtracted); 14,000 kJ applies 2 per cent to the total radiation instead of the PAR; 2,400 kJ is the respiratory loss.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity; energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option A: 5,600 kJ

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a food web, grass is eaten by grasshoppers and rabbits; frogs eat grasshoppers; snakes eat frogs and rabbits; and hawks eat snakes. Taking producers as the first trophic level, the snake occupies:

options.text: The third and fourth trophic levels at the same time
The second and third trophic levels

solution.concept: An organism at more than one trophic level
solution.explanation: Through grass → rabbit → snake, the snake is at the third trophic level (primary carnivore). Through grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, it is at the fourth (secondary carnivore). A species can occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time, because a trophic level is a functional level, not a species.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A and B each take only one of the two chains; the snake never eats producers, so it cannot be at the second level.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow: trophic levels
solution.final_answer: Option C: The third and fourth trophic levels at the same time

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Four samples of detritus are left to decompose under different conditions. Which is expected to decompose fastest?

options.text: Woody bark rich in lignin, in warm, moist, well-aerated soil
Nitrogen-rich leaf litter with plenty of soluble sugars, in warm, moist, well-aerated soil
Nitrogen-rich leaf litter with plenty of soluble sugars, in cold, waterlogged (anaerobic) soil
Insect exoskeletons rich in chitin, in cold, dry soil

solution.concept: Chemical and climatic control of decomposition
solution.explanation: Decomposition is quicker when detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances such as sugars, and slower when it is rich in lignin and chitin. A warm and moist environment favours decomposition, while low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit it; decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process. Both favourable factors occur together only in the keyed option.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A has resistant lignin; option C has good chemistry but cold, anaerobic conditions; option D has both resistant chitin and cold, dry conditions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option B: Nitrogen-rich leaf litter with plenty of soluble sugars, in warm, moist, well-aerated soil

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about a pond as an ecosystem are correct?

(a) A pond is a shallow water body in which all the basic components of an ecosystem are well exhibited.
(b) A pond is fairly a self-sustainable unit and a rather simple example that explains even the complex interactions in an aquatic ecosystem.
(c) Energy flow in a pond is cyclic: the heat released by consumers is reused by the autotrophs.
(d) A pond lacks decomposers because decomposition takes place only on land.
(e) The rate of function of the pond community is regulated by solar input, the cycle of temperature, day-length and other climatic conditions.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT uses the pond as a fairly self-sustainable and simple example of an aquatic ecosystem in which all the basic components are well exhibited. Its functioning depends on solar input, the temperature cycle, day-length and other climatic conditions. Energy flows in one direction towards higher trophic levels and is lost as heat; it is not recycled. Decomposers such as fungi, bacteria and flagellates are especially abundant at the bottom of the pond.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (c) or (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: For the species–area relationship, log S = log C + Z log A, NCERT notes that the value of Z for areas within a region is amazingly similar, regardless of the taxonomic group or the region. It lies in the range:

solution.explanation: Whether it is plants in Britain, birds in California or molluscs in New York state, the slopes (Z) of the regression lines are amazingly similar, in the range 0.1 to 0.2. Much steeper slopes (0.6 to 1.2) are found only when very large areas such as entire continents are analysed.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.6 to 1.2 is the range for very large areas such as continents; the other ranges are not given by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: species–area relationships
solution.final_answer: Option B: 0.1 to 0.2

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: In situ and ex situ conservation
questions.question_text: In many cultures, tracts of forest were set aside as sacred groves. In such groves:

options.text: Only commercially valuable timber trees are protected
Trees may be felled freely but wildlife is protected
All the trees and wildlife are venerated and given total protection
Exotic species are planted to raise productivity

solution.explanation: NCERT: in many cultures tracts of forest were set aside, and all the trees and wildlife within were venerated and given total protection. Such sacred groves are found in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya, the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan, the Western Ghat regions of Karnataka and Maharashtra, and the Sarguja, Chanda and Bastar areas of Madhya Pradesh. They are an in situ means of conservation.
steps: Sacred groves: total protection of all trees and wildlife
solution.why_others_wrong: Protection in sacred groves is total, not selective, and they preserve native vegetation rather than introducing exotic species.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: in situ conservation
solution.final_answer: Option C: All the trees and wildlife are venerated and given total protection

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: In situ and ex situ conservation
questions.question_text: Which statement about zoological parks as a means of conservation is correct according to NCERT?

options.text: They are a means of in situ conservation
They protect the whole ecosystem of the animals they keep
No animal that is extinct in the wild is kept in them
Many animals that have become extinct in the wild continue to be maintained in zoological parks

solution.explanation: Zoological parks, botanical gardens and wildlife safari parks are means of ex situ conservation, in which threatened species are taken out of their natural habitat and given special care. NCERT notes that many animals that have become extinct in the wild continue to be maintained in zoological parks.
steps: Some species extinct in the wild survive in zoos
solution.why_others_wrong: Zoos are ex situ, not in situ; they keep individual species, not whole ecosystems; option D contradicts NCERT's statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: ex situ conservation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Many animals that have become extinct in the wild continue to be maintained in zoological parks

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Careful analysis of records shows that extinctions across taxa are not random. Which group does NCERT mention as appearing more vulnerable to extinction?

solution.explanation: NCERT: extinctions across taxa are not random; some groups, like amphibians, appear to be more vulnerable to extinction.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT names amphibians, not insects, bacteria or fungi, as the more vulnerable group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Amphibians

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: In situ and ex situ conservation
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Biodiversity knows no political boundaries, and its conservation is therefore a collective responsibility of all nations.
Statement II: When we conserve and protect a whole ecosystem, its biodiversity at all levels is protected; for example, we save the entire forest to save the tiger.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: In situ conservation and global responsibility
solution.explanation: NCERT states that biodiversity knows no political boundaries and its conservation is a collective responsibility of all nations, as recognised at the Earth Summit (1992). It also explains in situ (on site) conservation: protecting the whole ecosystem protects biodiversity at all levels, e.g. saving the entire forest to save the tiger. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Loss of a key species that drives a major ecosystem function is a more serious threat to the ecosystem than the loss of a few other species.
Reason (R): A key species drives a major ecosystem function, so its removal disrupts that function for the whole ecosystem, whereas the functions of many other species overlap.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Paul Ehrlich compared an ecosystem to an airplane and species to its rivets. Removing rivets one by one may not affect flight safety at first, but over time the plane weakens. Which rivets are lost also matters: losing rivets on the wings (key species that drive major ecosystem functions) is a more serious threat than losing a few on the seats or windows. R is the reasoning that supports A.
steps: Wing rivets = key species → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity: importance of species diversity to the ecosystem
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the reasons for conserving biodiversity are correct?

(a) Industrial products such as tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins and perfumes illustrate the narrowly utilitarian argument.
(b) Aesthetic pleasures, such as walking through thick woods or waking up to a bulbul's song, are among the intangible benefits of the broadly utilitarian argument.
(c) About 25,000 species of plants contribute to the traditional medicines used by native peoples around the world.
(d) Pollination by bees, birds and bats is the standard example of the ethical argument.
(e) According to the ethical argument, species that have no current economic value need not be conserved.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Narrowly utilitarian: direct economic benefits, such as food, firewood, fibre and industrial products (tannins, lubricants, dyes, resins, perfumes), and medicines; 25,000 plant species contribute to traditional medicines. Broadly utilitarian: ecosystem services such as oxygen production and pollination, and intangible aesthetic pleasures. Ethical: every species has an intrinsic value, even if it has no current economic value, and we have a moral duty to care for it.
steps: (d): false, pollination is a broadly utilitarian service
(e): false, the ethical argument values every species
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: why should we conserve biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Biodiversity hotspots are regions with very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism. NCERT adds that they are also regions of:

solution.explanation: Hotspots are identified for very high species richness and high endemism, and NCERT notes that they are also regions of accelerated habitat loss. That is why strict protection of the hotspots could greatly reduce ongoing extinctions.
steps: Hotspot: high richness + endemism + accelerated habitat loss
solution.why_others_wrong: Hotspots have high, not low, species richness; they face accelerated habitat loss, so they are neither protected from human activity nor places of low extinction risk.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: hotspots
solution.final_answer: Option B: Accelerated habitat loss

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (symbol in log S = log C + Z log A) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. S
B. A
C. Z
D. C

List-II:
I. Y-intercept
II. Area
III. Slope of the line (regression coefficient)
IV. Species richness

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: On a logarithmic scale the species–area relationship is a straight line, log S = log C + Z log A, where S is species richness, A is area, Z is the slope of the line (regression coefficient) and C is the Y-intercept.
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A swaps S and A; option B swaps Z and C; option C swaps S and C.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: species–area relationships
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: For islands within one region, the species–area relationship follows log S = log C + Z log A with Z = 0.2. If island Q is 32 times larger in area than island P, how many times more species is island Q expected to have?

solution.explanation: log S = log C + Z log A means S = C·A^Z. So S_Q/S_P = (A_Q/A_P)^Z = 32^0.2. Since 32 = 2⁵, 32^0.2 = 2^(5 × 0.2) = 2¹ = 2.
solution.shortcut: Ratio of species = (ratio of areas)^Z.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.4 multiplies the area ratio by Z instead of raising it to the power Z; 32 assumes species are directly proportional to area (Z = 1); 1.2 simply adds Z to 1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: species–area relationships
solution.final_answer: Option C: 2 times

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the loss and conservation of biodiversity are correct?

(a) The 'Evil Quartet' consists of habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and pollution.
(b) When alien species are introduced, some of them turn invasive and cause the decline or extinction of indigenous species.
(c) Ex situ conservation protects the whole ecosystem in which a threatened species lives.
(d) Cryopreservation of gametes, in vitro fertilisation and tissue culture propagation help to conserve threatened species ex situ.
(e) Biosphere reserves are a means of ex situ conservation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Causes of loss and means of conservation
solution.explanation: The Evil Quartet is habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions (not pollution). Some introduced alien species turn invasive and cause decline or extinction of native species (e.g. Nile perch). Ex situ conservation takes threatened species out of their habitat; it does not protect whole ecosystems. It now includes cryopreservation of gametes, in vitro fertilisation and tissue culture. Biosphere reserves are in situ.
steps: (a): false, the fourth cause is co-extinctions
solution.why_others_wrong: Option B adds (a), option C adds (c), and option D contains only false statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity: causes; biodiversity conservation
solution.final_answer: Option A: (b) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: animals whose cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are diploblastic, e.g. coelenterates; an undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present between them. Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
