questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cells sloughed from tumours reach distant sites through blood, and wherever they get lodged in the body they start a new tumour.
Statement II: Proto-oncogenes (cellular oncogenes) are present only in cancer cells and never in normal cells.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cells sloughed from malignant tumours reach distant sites through blood, and wherever they get lodged they start a new tumour (metastasis). Genes called cellular oncogenes (c-onc) or proto-oncogenes have been identified in normal cells; when activated under certain conditions, they could lead to oncogenic transformation of the cells.
steps: Statement II: false - proto-oncogenes are identified in normal cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II contradicts NCERT's 'identified in normal cells', so options A and D are wrong; Statement I is NCERT, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Cancer

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, which of the following is NOT among the causes that motivate youth towards drug and alcohol use?

options.text: Curiosity, need for adventure and excitement, and experimentation
A stable and supportive family structure
Using drugs to escape facing problems

solution.explanation: NCERT: curiosity, need for adventure and excitement, and experimentation are common causes; the child may later use drugs to escape facing problems; peer pressure and unstable or unsupportive family structures also contribute. A stable, supportive family is protective, not a cause.
steps: Causes: curiosity, adventure, experimentation, escaping problems, peer pressure
Unstable families contribute; a stable, supportive family does not

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cancerous cells give rise to masses of cells called tumours.
Reason (R): Cancerous cells have lost the property of contact inhibition and just continue to divide.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Normal cells stop dividing on contact with other cells (contact inhibition). NCERT: cancerous cells appear to have lost this property; as a result they just continue to divide, giving rise to masses of cells called tumours. R explains A.
steps: Loss of contact inhibition -> continued division -> tumour
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the cause of A in NCERT's account, so B is wrong; both are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Cancer
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (disease) with List-II (type of pathogen).

List-I:
A. Typhoid
B. Amoebiasis
C. Ascariasis
D. Ringworm

List-II:
I. Protozoan
II. Fungi
III. Bacterium
IV. Helminth

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi; amoebiasis by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica; ascariasis by the helminth (roundworm) Ascaris; ringworm by fungi such as Microsporum, Trichophyton and Epidermophyton.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes call typhoid protozoan, ringworm a worm, or amoebiasis a helminth disease.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common diseases in humans
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Restriction endonucleases recognise palindromic sequences, which read the same on the two strands of DNA when the orientation of reading is kept the same (5' to 3'). Which of the following double-stranded sequences, given as its upper (5' to 3') strand, is a palindrome?

solution.explanation: A sequence is palindromic if its complementary strand, read 5' to 3', is the same. For 5'-GGATCC-3' the complementary strand is 3'-CCTAGG-5', which read 5' to 3' is GGATCC - identical. The other sequences give different sequences when the complementary strand is read 5' to 3'.
solution.shortcut: The second half must be the complement of the first half read backwards: GGA|TCC.
solution.why_others_wrong: GATCTC reads GAGATC on the other strand, AAGCTA reads TAGCTT and GGAACC reads GGTTCC; none is the same on both strands.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 5'-GGATCC-3'

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), the DNA polymerase extends the primers using:

options.text: Amino acids provided in the reaction and mRNA as template
The nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template
Ribosomes of the host cell and tRNA

solution.explanation: NCERT: in PCR, the enzyme extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template. A thermostable polymerase is used so that it survives the high-temperature denaturation.
steps: Polymerase adds nucleotides supplied in the reaction, copying the genomic DNA template
solution.why_others_wrong: Amino acids, ribosomes and tRNA are used in protein synthesis, not DNA synthesis; restriction enzymes and ligase cut and join DNA but do not copy it.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option B: The nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, bioreactors can be thought of as vessels in which:

options.text: DNA is cut into fragments and separated by size
DNA is amplified in vitro by repeated cycles of heating and cooling
Raw materials are biologically converted into specific products using microbial, plant, animal or human cells
Bacterial cells are made competent with calcium ions

solution.explanation: NCERT: bioreactors can be thought of as vessels in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products, individual enzymes, etc., using microbial, plant, animal or human cells.
steps: Raw materials -> products by biological conversion
Uses microbial, plant, animal or human cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Cutting and separating DNA describes restriction digestion and gel electrophoresis, amplification is PCR, and making cells competent is a transformation step.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Obtaining the foreign gene product
solution.final_answer: Option C: Raw materials are biologically converted into specific products using microbial, plant, animal or human cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Retroviruses are used to develop vectors for animal cells because, in animals, retroviruses have the ability to:

options.text: Deliver T-DNA into dicot plant cells
Cut DNA at specific palindromic sites
Remain active at the high temperatures used in PCR
Transform normal cells into cancerous cells

solution.explanation: NCERT: retroviruses in animals have the ability to transform normal cells into cancerous cells. Disarmed retroviruses are now used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells.
steps: Natural ability: transform normal cells into cancerous cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Delivering T-DNA is the property of Agrobacterium tumefaciens, cutting at palindromes is done by restriction enzymes, and heat stability belongs to Taq polymerase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option D: Transform normal cells into cancerous cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A piece of alien DNA moved into an organism usually cannot multiply in the progeny cells. When it becomes integrated into the genome of the recipient, it may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA because:

options.text: It has been cut into sticky ends by a restriction enzyme
It has become part of a chromosome, which has the ability to replicate
It has been stained with ethidium bromide
It has been converted into protein by the host cell

solution.concept: Why alien DNA must join a replicon
solution.explanation: NCERT: when the alien piece of DNA becomes part of a chromosome, which has the ability to replicate, it is replicated and inherited along with the host DNA. A chromosome carries an origin of replication, responsible for initiating replication.
steps: Free alien DNA cannot replicate on its own
Once part of a chromosome (with ori) it replicates with it
solution.why_others_wrong: Sticky ends allow joining, staining allows viewing, and translation makes protein; none of these lets the DNA replicate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Principles of biotechnology
solution.final_answer: Option B: It has become part of a chromosome, which has the ability to replicate

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: After agarose gel electrophoresis, the separated DNA bands are cut out and the DNA is extracted (elution). According to NCERT, the purified DNA fragments are then used in:

options.text: Constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors
Measuring the copy number of a plasmid

solution.explanation: NCERT: the separated bands of DNA are cut out from the agarose gel and extracted from the gel piece (elution). The DNA fragments purified in this way are used in constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors.
steps: Purified fragment joined with a cloning vector -> recombinant DNA
solution.why_others_wrong: Competence is induced with divalent cations, copy number is a property of the vector, and ethidium bromide is a stain added from outside; none is what eluted DNA is used for.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Separation and isolation of DNA fragments
solution.final_answer: Option B: Constructing recombinant DNA by joining them with cloning vectors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A gene is cloned into a plasmid whose copy number is 20 per cell. A culture contains 5 × 10^5 transformed bacterial cells, each carrying the recombinant plasmid at this copy number. How many copies of the cloned gene are present in the culture?

solution.concept: Copy number and amplification of cloned DNA
solution.explanation: NCERT: if an alien piece of DNA is linked with plasmid DNA, its number can be multiplied to the copy number of the plasmid. With 20 plasmids per cell and 5 × 10^5 cells: 20 × 5 × 10^5 = 1 × 10^7 copies.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 × 10^5 assumes one copy per cell, 2.5 × 10^4 divides by the copy number instead of multiplying, and 1 × 10^6 slips a power of ten.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option C: 1 × 10^7

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Restriction enzyme digestions are performed by incubating purified DNA molecules with the restriction enzyme under the optimal conditions for that specific enzyme.
Statement II: Sticky ends are so named because they form covalent bonds with their complementary cut counterparts.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: restriction enzyme digestions are performed by incubating purified DNA with the enzyme at the optimal conditions for that specific enzyme. Sticky ends are named so because they form hydrogen bonds (not covalent bonds) with their complementary cut counterparts; DNA ligase then seals the backbone.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II replaces hydrogen bonds with covalent bonds, so options A and D are wrong; Statement I is NCERT, so B is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Processes of recombinant DNA technology; Restriction enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Plasmids and bacteriophages are used as cloning vectors.
Reason (R): Plasmids and bacteriophages have the ability to replicate within bacterial cells independent of the control of chromosomal DNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why plasmids and phages are vectors
solution.explanation: NCERT: plasmids and bacteriophages have the ability to replicate within bacterial cells independent of the control of chromosomal DNA. So a foreign DNA linked to them is replicated too, which is why they are used as cloning vectors.
steps: Independent replication carries the linked foreign DNA along -> vector
solution.why_others_wrong: R is the property that makes them vectors, so B is wrong; both are true, so C and D are wrong.

questions.subject: Zoology

Identification of DNA with desirable genes -> introduction of the identified DNA into the host -> maintenance of the introduced DNA in the host and its transfer to the progeny
Identification of DNA with desirable genes -> maintenance in the host -> introduction into the host

solution.explanation: NCERT: there are three basic steps in genetically modifying an organism - (i) identification of DNA with desirable genes; (ii) introduction of the identified DNA into the host; (iii) maintenance of the introduced DNA in the host and transfer of the DNA to its progeny.
steps: 3: maintain it and pass it to progeny
solution.why_others_wrong: A gene must be identified before it can be introduced, and it can be maintained in the host only after it has been introduced; each wrong option breaks this order.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A PCR starts with a single double-stranded DNA molecule. Every new DNA strand is synthesised by extension of one primer, and each cycle copies every strand present. After 3 cycles, how many primer molecules have been incorporated into DNA?

solution.explanation: After n cycles there are 2^n double-stranded molecules, i.e., 2^(n+1) strands. Only the 2 original template strands were not made by extending a primer; every other strand begins with one primer. For n = 3: 2^4 = 16 strands, so 16 - 2 = 14 primers are incorporated.
solution.shortcut: Primers used = (2 × number of molecules) - 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 counts double-stranded molecules, 16 counts all strands including the two original template strands, and 6 assumes only two primers per cycle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Amplification of gene of interest using PCR
solution.final_answer: Option D: 14

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Foreign DNA is ligated at the PstI site of pBR322, which lies within the ampicillin resistance gene, and E. coli is transformed. Which of the following correctly describes the growth of transformants?

options.text: Recombinants grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin; non-recombinant transformants grow on both
Recombinants grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline; non-recombinant transformants grow on neither
Recombinants and non-recombinant transformants both grow on ampicillin and tetracycline
Recombinants grow on neither antibiotic, because the plasmid is destroyed by the insert

solution.concept: Insertional inactivation of the ampicillin resistance gene
solution.explanation: Inserting foreign DNA within a gene inactivates it (insertional inactivation). Recombinant plasmids lose ampicillin resistance but keep the intact tetracycline resistance gene. Non-recombinant plasmids keep both genes. Untransformed cells have neither resistance.
steps: Insert in ampR -> ampR inactivated in recombinants
solution.why_others_wrong: The first wrong option is the BamHI (tetR) situation reversed; the second ignores insertional inactivation; the third forgets that the tetracycline resistance gene remains intact.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors
solution.final_answer: Option A: Recombinants grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin; non-recombinant transformants grow on both

The Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens has been modified into a cloning vector that is no longer pathogenic to plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes give the copy-number problem the calcium treatment, the plant problem the colour marker, or the selection problem the high-copy vector.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors; Competent host (for transformation with recombinant DNA)

Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why the same enzyme is used
solution.explanation: NCERT: when cut by the same restriction enzyme, the resultant DNA fragments have the same kind of sticky ends, and these can be joined together (end-to-end) using DNA ligase. Normally, unless one cuts the vector and the source DNA with the same restriction enzyme, the recombinant vector molecule cannot be created.
steps: Matching sticky ends (R) are why the same enzyme is needed (A)
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the reason for A, so B is wrong; both are NCERT statements, so C and D are wrong.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about isolating and joining DNA are correct?

(a) DNA is enclosed within membranes, so the cell has to be broken open to release it.
(b) When the cell is broken open, DNA is released along with RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and lipids.
(c) Ribonuclease is used to remove the proteins from the DNA preparation.
(d) The cut 'gene of interest' and the cut vector are mixed and DNA ligase is added to prepare recombinant DNA.
(e) DNA ligase cuts DNA at specific recognition sequences.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: since DNA is enclosed within membranes, the cell has to be broken open, releasing DNA along with RNA, proteins, polysaccharides and lipids. RNA is removed by ribonuclease and proteins by protease. After cutting, the gene of interest and the cut vector are mixed and ligase is added to give recombinant DNA. Cutting at recognition sequences is done by restriction enzymes, not ligase.
steps: (e) False: ligase joins, it does not cut
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) gives ribonuclease the job of protease and (e) gives ligase the job of a restriction enzyme; every other option includes one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Isolation of the genetic material (DNA); Processes of recombinant DNA technology

questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events by which the Bt toxin kills an insect?

Ingestion of inactive protoxin -> binding to midgut cells -> solubilisation by alkaline pH -> activation -> death
Ingestion of inactive protoxin -> solubilisation by alkaline gut pH and activation -> binding to midgut epithelial cells and pore formation -> swelling and lysis of cells -> death of the insect

solution.concept: Mode of action of Bt toxin
solution.explanation: The Bt toxin exists as an inactive protoxin. Once the insect ingests it, the alkaline pH of the gut solubilises the crystals and the toxin becomes active. steps: Two DNA sequences: chain A and chain B
Introduced into E. coli plasmids; chains made separately
solution.why_others_wrong: Mature insulin lacks the C peptide and was made in E. coli, not Agrobacterium; animal pancreas was the older source that recombinant insulin replaced; the chains are joined by disulphide bonds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in medicine (genetically engineered insulin)
solution.final_answer: Option B: DNA sequences for chains A and B were introduced into plasmids of E. coli; the chains were made separately, extracted and combined by creating disulphide bonds
